scenes.name: The Slits
scenes.book: Postpunk. Romper todo y empezar de nuevo
scenes.author: Simon Reynolds
scenes.desc: Una pandilla de chicas montaraces (Ari Up, Viv Albertine, Tessa Pollitt, Palmolive) que empezó genuinamente inepta y mejoró al aprender lo básico y encontrar un groove reggae con Budgie. Tras librarse de Malcolm McLaren, graban Cut (Island, 1979) con Dennis Bovell: engranajes polirrítmicos, la guitarra rítmica de Albertine («una versión femenina de Steve Cropper») y voces que se superponen en geometrías extrañas. Canciones sobre consumismo, romance y alienación («Typical Girls», «Shoplifting», «Newtown»); la portada, Amazonas embadurnadas de barro. Forman con The Pop Group una tribu y el sello Y; «In the Beginning There Was Rhythm», influida por el primer hip hop, y Return of the Giant Slits (CBS) cierran la historia.
scenes.family: Vanguardia postpunk: dub, funk y política

scenes.name: The Raincoats
scenes.book: Postpunk. Romper todo y empezar de nuevo
scenes.author: Simon Reynolds
scenes.desc: Formadas por Gina Birch y Ana da Silva tras una envidia «estimulante» de The Slits, con Palmolive y la violinista Vicky Aspinall: feminismo sin glamour, ropa ordinaria y conciertos tímidos que el público parecía espiar (Kurt Cobain). Aprendieron a tocar sobre la marcha; un punk desaliñado con tintes de folk («Off Duty Trip»). Odyshape (1981) es el postpunk despojado del rock: balafón, kalimba, bajo libre y percusiones añadidas por Charles Hayward y Robert Wyatt.

podcast.title: Contribution to The Slits and The Raincoats
podcast.body: Although Paloma Romero (Palmolive) did not appear on any records by The Slits after leaving the band, several of her songs were used. She then moved on to join The Raincoats, another influential all-female punk band highly praised by Kurt Cobain. "Palmolev never appeared on any slits records. She'd quit the band by then, but several of her songs were used. Instead, she moved on and joined the raincoats, another all-female band, and one of Kurt Cobain's all-time favorite groups."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Driven By Her: History of Female Drummers

podcast.title: Early Punk Drummer and Quick Learning
podcast.body: Paloma Romero, a Spanish-born drummer, became a key figure in the early UK punk scene. Inspired by the movement, she learned to play drums in just one week before joining The Slits, an all-female band she co-founded with two 14-year-olds. "The whole scene inspired her to learn how to play the drums. She says she practiced for a whole week to learn how to play them. And then she joined an all-female band with a couple of 14-year-olds and they became the slits."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Driven By Her: History of Female Drummers

podcast.title: Relationship with Joe Strummer
podcast.body: Paloma Romero was romantically involved with John Miller, who later became known as Joe Strummer. This connection highlights her presence within the tight-knit early punk community in the UK. "She had a boyfriend named John Miller, who later changed his name to Joe Strummer."
